rationale: After the 'Principles and Scope of Demography' content block, checks comprehension of the difference between formal and social demography — a core conceptual distinction introduced in that block.

After the 'Using Vital Statistics: Quality Assessment' content block, reinforces the key fact (from the clinical pearl block at index 10) that the SRS — not the Civil Registration System — is the benchmarking gold standard for vital rates in India.

After the 'Fertility Indices: Measurement and Interpretation' content block, tests the ability to identify the correct denominator and hierarchy among CBR, GFR, and TFR — a common exam and clinical confusion point.

After the 'Sex Ratio, Child Sex Ratio, and Causes of Decline' content block, tests accurate recall of the operational definition of child sex ratio as used in Census 2011 — a fact students frequently confuse with the overall sex ratio.
After the 'National Population Policy 2000: Framework and Goals' content block, tests accurate recall of the NPP-2000 TFR target — a high-yield fact in Community Medicine examinations.

After the 'Applying Population Policy Concepts to Community Practice' content block, reinforces the distinction between contraceptive failure (contraceptive methods prevent conception) and post-fertilisation methods — aligned with the clinical pearl at index 10 about emergency contraception.
